description: About Etched Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across prefill and decode. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, we're redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history. Job Summary Core Engineering is our special projects team. This team identifies critical gaps across Etched and builds solutions 0 to 1, often in days, with immediate feedback loops. You might build internal tools to unblock a hardware team, prototype systems for manufacturing execution, or design, evaluate, and deploy agentic systems for our most challenging R&D problems. This role is for engineers who thrive on ambiguity, move fast without sacrificing quality, and get energy from solving whatever problem matters most right now. It is a whiteboard for future founders – if you're interested in shipping 0-1 production-level code every week, this role is for you. This role requires exceptional full-stack engineering capabilities, deep product sense, personal accountability, and a knack for building from the ground up. At Etched, we're developing our processes for scale, and we're looking for engineers to deploy to our toughest challenges. The problems we solve are time-sensitive and business-critical. This role will not be a 9-5, and the ideal candidate is excited about that. This is not a shadowing program. You will own a real project, scoped to land in production and shape how Etched executes. You may be a good fit if you: Have a track record of solving hard problems across stacks and domains — you enjoy being dropped into unfamiliar territory and figuring it out Have something you built that you can walk us through in depth. Depth in one thing beats a list of ten Are comfortable with Python and TypeScript: you can read it, modify it, debug it, and direct AI to write it well. We don't care whether you write code from scratch, but we do care whether you ship things that work Have product sense and its necessary prerequisites, from AI tooling proficiency to design taste Bias towards action and comfort with incomplete information Strong candidates may also have: Data engineering, infrastructure or DevOps experience, and deploying operational systems in enterprise environments Experience wielding frontier models on frontier problems: an eval-driven mindset — you measure whether AI systems work, identify where they fall short, and know how to hillclimb High agency and comfort with ambiguity — you find the real problem to solve Prior startup experience, especially during hyper growth We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification Program details 12-week paid internship (June - August 2026) Generous housing support for those relocating Daily lunch and dinner in our office Based at our office in San Jose, CA Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time For any questions, contact internships@etched.com How we're different Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson . We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference. We are a fully in-person team in San Jose and Taipei, and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

description: Company Overview ACS (Allen Control Systems) is a defense technology company building precision robotic systems for the United States and its allies. Founded by two former U.S. Navy electrical engineers with deep experience in robotics and software, ACS brings together AI, computer vision, precision motion, and advanced hardware to solve complex defense challenges across land, air, and maritime environments. Our flagship product, Bullfrog, is an autonomous precision weapon system that transforms existing weapons into highly accurate counter-drone systems — giving warfighters a scalable, cost-effective response to one of the fastest-growing threats on the modern battlefield. Bullfrog is deployed with U.S. forces, and ACS works with organizations throughout the U.S. military and national security community. Following a $200 million Series B at a $2.2 billion valuation, ACS is rapidly expanding manufacturing, accelerating Bullfrog deployments, and developing the next generation of autonomous battlefield systems. This is an opportunity to join a proven, fast-moving team and help scale technology with direct, real-world impact on national security. ACS is headquartered in Austin, Texas, with additional operations in Alexandria, Virginia; Mountain View, California; and Huntsville, Alabama. For more information, visit allencontrolsystems.com . Our interns aren't fetching coffee or shadowing — they're working alongside the same engineers and product teams building the systems we ship. As an Android Developer Intern, you'll help design and improve the interfaces that connect people with real-time technology, from mobile and embedded applications to internal tools used by our engineering and operations teams. This is early-career work with real stakes. You'll work closely with engineers, product managers, and other designers to turn complex technical systems into interfaces that are intuitive, responsive, and built for the people who use them. Location: Austin, TX (on-site) Duration: Summer 2027 (~10–12 weeks) Pay: Paid Internship (to be discussed during interviews) What You'll Do Design and iterate on user interfaces for Android, tablet, embedded, and internal applications. Work closely with engineers to bring designs to life using technologies such as Jetpack Compose and modern Android UI frameworks. Collaborate with product managers, software engineers, and other stakeholders to understand user needs and translate them into thoughtful design solutions. Design for real-time systems where responsiveness, clarity, and reliability matter. Explore interaction patterns for touchscreens, gamepads/controllers, and other input methods. Help establish and maintain consistent UI patterns and design systems across applications. Participate in user feedback, usability testing, and iterative design reviews. Communicate design decisions clearly and incorporate feedback from both technical and non-technical teammates. What We're Looking For Currently pursuing a degree in UI Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design, Computer Science, Software Engineering , or a related field. Coursework, project, or internship experience in UI/UX design, interaction design, product design, or Android mobile development. A portfolio or examples of work demonstrating your approach to solving user problems through design. This can include class projects, personal projects, apps, prototypes, or previous internships. An interest in designing interfaces for technical, real-time, or complex systems. Strong attention to detail and an instinct for creating simple, intuitive user experiences. Curiosity about how software is built and a willingness to work closely with engineers. Basic understanding of software development concepts and how UI connects to application logic. A builder's mindset: you'd rather create something, get feedback, and iterate than wait for a perfect spec. Strong communication skills and the ability to explain the thinking behind your design decisions. You'll Stand Out Experience designing interfaces for mobile, tablet, embedded, or real-time applications . Experience with Android, Jetpack Compose, Kotlin, or other mobile development technologies . Experience designing for game-like interactions, simulations, controllers, or other non-traditional input methods. Experience collaborating directly with software engineers to implement designs. Interest in embedded systems, robotics, autonomy, or other technically complex products. Why ACS Direct impact: Your work contributes to products that are built for real-world use — not stuck in a slide deck. Real ownership: You'll work directly with the engineers and product team building Bullfrog and contribute to real product decisions from day one. Small team, big scope: At a startup this size, interns take on meaningful problems and see their work move from concept to implementation. Cross-functional experience: Work alongside designers, product managers, and engineers to understand what it takes to build and ship a product. Mentorship: Learn from experienced engineers and product builders who have designed and fielded real defense systems.

description: Wheeled Platforms & Lifting Systems Emeryville, California | Internship Proposed base compensation. Final terms are subject to Astera’s hiring process. Position Summary Help us build and compare the systems that allow robots to move and adjust their working height. Under engineering mentorship, you will prototype wheeled mobile bases and lifting platforms, run hands-on experiments, and evaluate how different designs perform under realistic operating conditions. Starting with our existing hoverboard hub motors and other motorized wheel hardware, you will help explore different wheel and drivetrain configurations. You will also help develop and evaluate lifting platforms, comparing commercially available mechanisms and custom prototypes. Your work will help the team select practical designs based on measured performance, reliability, cost, and ease of integration. Core Responsibilities Evaluate wheeled platforms. Assemble and modify mobile bases using hoverboard hub motors, hub motor wheels, and conventional motor-driven wheel assemblies. Help design and fabricate chassis, mounts, and supporting components. Compare navigation performance of different systems. Compare wheel and drivetrain configurations. Develop repeatable tests to evaluate maneuverability, low-speed motion, traction, payload handling, power consumption, steerability and general performance across relevant floor surfaces. Prototype lifting platforms. Help assemble, adapt, and test different lifting mechanisms, such as scissor lifts and telescoping lifting columns. Integrate actuators, guides, mounts, and supporting structures. Evaluate lifting performance. Compare lifting range, speed, positioning repeatability, rigidity, and stability under defined loads. Investigate vibration, mechanical play, and other issues that affect reliable operation. Integrate controls and measurements. Configure motor controllers, connect position and speed feedback, and develop simple control and data-collection scripts. Help implement travel limits, homing, and coordinated motion under engineering supervision. Document comparisons and improve designs. Maintain CAD files, wiring diagrams, parts lists, and test records. Summarize tradeoffs and work with engineers to refine promising designs. Keep experimental hardware ready. Organize components, tools, and spares; maintain prototypes and test fixtures; and assist with equipment inspections, repairs, and experiment setup. Required Qualifications Coursework, projects, or practical experience in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, robotics, mechatronics, or a related discipline. Experience building and troubleshooting a physical system through coursework, research, student teams, or personal projects. Basic familiarity with mechanical assembly, electrical wiring, motors, and sensors. Interest in hands-on prototyping and systematic testing, including careful measurement and documentation. Comfort working with an engineering mentor and contributing to the upkeep of a shared robotics lab. Preferred Experience CAD, 3D printing, machining, or fabrication of mechanical prototypes. BLDC motors, motor controllers, encoders, wheeled robots, or drivetrain design. Linear actuators, screw drives, scissor lifts, lifting columns, or other positioning mechanisms. Python, C/C++, microcontrollers, or basic feedback control. Building test fixtures, collecting experimental data, or comparing hardware designs. Prior experience with every technology listed is not expected. We value curiosity, practical problem-solving, and an interest in understanding how different mechanical systems perform through real experiments.

description: About Base Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time. About the Role As a Power Systems Engineering Intern on Base’s Risk & Trading team, you’ll help model how our network of distributed residential batteries interacts with the grid, at both the distribution and transmission levels. During your internship you’ll be tasked with important problems for the business and expected to deliver just like any other full-time member of the team. You’ll work alongside Base’s power systems engineers on power flow studies, grid models, and the analysis behind where our batteries are deployed and how they’re dispatched. This is hands-on engineering work with real stakeholders. The studies and tools you build will be used by Base’s operations and business development teams and can shape how we work with utilities and grid operators. You’ll own a scoped project end to end, from defining the study and building the model to presenting what you found. What You’ll Do Help design and run power flow studies (e.g., steady-state and contingency analyses) for Base battery aggregation use cases. Build and validate distribution and transmission system models, using standard test topologies such as the IEEE test feeders. Write Python to automate studies so they can be solved programmatically and run on a recurring basis. Analyze and visualize study results and grid data, and turn them into clear recommendations, such as where on a feeder Base’s systems create the most value. Compile and present your results to power systems engineers and the broader Risk & Trading team. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or a related technical field. Coursework, research, or project experience in power systems: power flow, per-unit systems, and three-phase analysis. Proficiency in Python for data analysis and visualization (e.g., pandas, NumPy, matplotlib). A strong foundation in linear algebra and numerical methods (e.g., Newton-Raphson). A strong ownership mindset and the ability to clearly explain your assumptions, methods, and results. Nice to have: exposure to power flow tools such as OpenDSS, GridLAB-D, CYME, PSS/E, PowerWorld, PyPSA, or pandapower, or to optimal power flow and electricity markets (e.g., ERCOT). About the Team Base’s Risk & Trading team is tasked with ensuring the grid-support performance and profitability of Base’s distributed battery fleet. This encompasses device communications with balancing authorities, telemetry analysis, algorithms for fleet aggregation and economic dispatch, through to financial portfolio management in wholesale energy markets. Our power systems engineers are the team’s experts on how the fleet interacts with the grid, from distribution feeders to the bulk transmission system. description: About Gen: Gen is a global company dedicated to powering Digital Freedom through its trusted consumer brands including Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion and more. Our combined heritage is rooted in financial empowerment and cyber safety for the first digital generations, and today we deliver award-winning cybersecurity, online privacy, identity protection and financial wellness solutions to nearly 500 million users in more than 150 countries. Together, we share a collective passion and vision to protect consumers and help them grow, manage and secure their digital and financial lives. We’re always looking for smart, fearless and high-impact talent who see AI as a teammate – leveraging it to move faster and deliver meaningful results. When you’re part of Gen, you’ll have the flexibility, tools and support to do your best work and grow your career – from flexible working options and time off to competitive pay, benefits and well-being programs. At Gen, we are scrappy and relentlessly customer driven. We create room for healthy debate, experimentation and continuous learning, and we seek out people with different experiences, identities and ideas to join our team. You’ll work with people who back each other, respect each other and understand that our differences are a competitive advantage. If this sounds like you, we’d love you to be part of Gen. About the Role: A suspicious web redirect is often just one step in a much larger chain. A traffic distribution system (TDS) decides where a visitor goes next based on signals such as their browser, location, referrer, or previous activity. In malicious campaigns, this can make the infrastructure difficult to observe and the final destination difficult to reach consistently. In this student position, you will investigate TDS infrastructure, understand its routing logic, and develop tools to capture browser activity, reconstruct redirection chains, and map the relationships between their components. The aim is to build a reusable approach to understanding how different TDS instances route visitors from an entry point to a final destination. The work will form the basis of your diploma thesis at Gen. With guidance from the team, you will develop your malware analysis and reverse engineering skills while using AI to help build and validate tooling for TDS research. Key Responsibilities: Analyze TDS infrastructure and investigate how it routes malicious traffic Reverse engineer and deobfuscate JavaScript to understand routing and evasion techniques Inspect and modify HTTP traffic, including headers, cookies, and redirects, using Chrome DevTools, Fiddler, Burp Suite, or similar tools Use AI to help develop and validate tools in JavaScript, Python, or other scripting languages for automated analysis and infrastructure mapping Test your findings and document the methods and results in your diploma thesis Perform other duties as instructed by your supervisor Interview Structure: The following steps have already been completed for the current candidate: Two discussions, one 60-minute session and one 30-minute session, covering the student's current skills, the homework assignment, mutual expectations, and the initial thesis direction A practical homework assignment, which the student successfully passed Initial alignment on a TDS-related diploma thesis; the detailed research question, deliverables, and evaluation criteria remain to be defined together

description: Quantitative Analyst Intern - Digital Assets Market Making (HFT) - Brussels Since 2017, Keyrock has been a change-maker in digital assets. We're a global, remote-first team of 200+ people across 40+ nationalities, with hubs in Brussels, London, Paris and New York. We provide liquidity across 80+ centralized and decentralized exchanges - a position cemented by our Series C, led by SC Ventures. Today we run a full spectrum of capital markets businesses across centralized and on-chain venues: market making, high-frequency trading, options, OTC, DeFi trading desks, advisory, and asset management. We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement. We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it. About the Internship Program Our internship programme gives early-career talent the opportunity to build practical skills, contribute to meaningful projects and learn alongside experienced colleagues in digital finance. Typically lasting six months and based in our Brussels office (London possible), each internship includes hands-on experience, clear learning goals and dedicated guidance and regular feedback. We look for curiosity, relevant foundational skills, deep, active interest and passion for digital assets and the potential to grow exponentially with us - you don’t need to arrive with all the answers. Where performance, business needs and available opportunities align, an internship may lead to a permanent role, though this is not guaranteed. We are looking for 3-4 high-caliber Quantitative Analyst Interns to sit within our Strategic Market Making (CeFi and DeFi), Credit and Corporate Development desks/teams (see other openings on our career page for details). Application deadline: 30 November 2026 Start date: 1 March 2027 Selection process: Interview with Talent Acquisition representative Interview with Hiring Manager Recruitment Challenge The role About Strategic Market Making Desk Our Strategic Proprietary Market Making team researches and deploys systematic trading strategies across centralized digital asset venues. We study how order-book dynamics, fragmented liquidity, exchange design and participant behaviour shape pricing, execution and risk. As a Quantitative Analyst Intern within the HFT track, you will work alongside quantitative researchers, traders and engineers to analyse market and trading data, test hypotheses through backtesting and simulation, and build tools that improve strategy performance and risk visibility. You will investigate how fair value, liquidity, latency, queue position, fees and adverse selection affect real-world execution across venues. This is a technical and applied internship. We are looking for someone who combines strong quantitative reasoning and coding skills with a detailed understanding of electronic markets. You should be curious about how exchanges work beneath the interface and able to connect market microstructure to trading outcomes. Key Responsibilities - Quantitative Analyst (HFT) Analyse multi-venue top-of-book and depth data, trades, orders, fills and cancels to study liquidity, price discovery and execution quality. Build and validate latency-aware, event-driven backtests with explicit assumptions around maker/taker execution, queue position, fill probability, fees and cancellations. Measure spread capture, forward markouts, fees and adverse selection, and investigate how execution quality changes across venues, instruments and market regimes. Build reusable Python tools and data pipelines using modern columnar analysis and SQL for strategy research, performance attribution and monitoring. Study cross-venue price discovery, lead–lag relationships, fair-value construction and spot–perpetual basis while accounting for data staleness, instrument design and settlement-currency differences. Support live strategies through PnL, inventory and exposure analysis, post-trade review and investigation of unexpected performance. Evaluate liquidity-program economics by balancing execution quality, market share, fees and incentives, and work with traders and engineers to translate research into robust production improvements. Present findings clearly, including assumptions, limitations, risks and recommended next steps. Who You Are/Key Requirements - Quantitative Analyst (HFT) Quantitative and coding foundations: You are pursuing or recently completed a degree in mathematics, computer science, engineering, physics, quantitative finance or a related field. You are proficient in Python for data analysis, ideally including Polars or similar columnar tools, and comfortable with SQL, Git and command-line workflows. Experience with ClickHouse or another analytical database is valuable. Electronic market structure: You understand limit order books, order types, maker/taker mechanics, matching and priority rules, spreads, market depth and how trades move prices. Execution awareness: You can reason about the order lifecycle from signal to acknowledgement and fill, including exchange APIs, latency, queue position, partial fills, cancellations, fees, slippage and adverse selection. Digital asset markets: You understand key differences between spot and perpetual futures, including basis, funding, leverage, liquidation risk, settlement currencies and residual exposure. description: Company Overview Lydian is developing the lowest cost sustainable fuels from waste CO2, water, and renewable electricity to decarbonize the aviation industry. You will take on hands-on engineering challenges—from understanding a process and developing concepts to designing in SolidWorks, selecting components, and building and testing prototypes. Your initial projects will focus on developing tooling and machinery for catalyst loading in our pilot reactor, including automated indexing, injection, and inspection. Develop and compare mechanical and mechatronic design concepts, then create SolidWorks models, assemblies, and drawings for selected designs. Test equipment, troubleshoot issues, analyze results, and use what you learn to improve designs and demonstrate reliable operation. Contribute to the development of catalyst-loading equipment, progressing from pilot-scale tooling toward full-scale systems. Collaborate with engineers and scientists across the team to incorporate project requirements and solve technical problems. Some hands-on experience with mechatronics design through coursework, projects, internships, or work—for example, robotics or automated manufacturing equipment. Experience using SolidWorks or comparable 3D CAD software to develop parts and assemblies; ability to turn a design concept into a buildable model. Able to understand an open-ended technical problem, develop and compare ideas, and make progress through hands-on design, building, and testing. Interest or experience in specifying and selecting mechanical and electrical components for a system. Comfortable working hands-on in a lab, shop, or prototyping environment, with attention to safety and detail. Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting design choices and sharing test results. Curiosity, eagerness to learn, and a proactive, collaborative approach to solving technical problems. Desire to work in a fast-paced environment and solve interesting technical problems. Experience with fabrication, machining, 3D printing, electrical wiring, or controls programming is a plus, but not required. description: 🎨 OpusClip is the world's No.1 AI video agent, built for authenticity on social media. We envision a world where everyone can authentically share their story through video, with no expertise needed. Within just 18 months of our launch, over 20 million creators and businesses have used OpusClip to enhance their social presence. We have raised $50 million in total funding and are fortunate to have some of the most supportive investors, including SoftBank Vision Fund, DCM Ventures, Millennium New Horizons, Fellows Fund, AI Grant, Jason Lemkin (SaaStr), Samsung Next, GTMfund, Alumni Ventures, and many more. Check out our latest coverage by Business Insider featuring our product and funding milestones, and our recognition as one of The Information's 50 Most Promising Startups in 2024. Headquartered in Mountain View, we are a team of 100 passionate and experienced AI enthusiasts and video experts, driven by our core values: Be a Champion Team Prioritize Ruthlessly Ship fast, Quality Follows Obsess over customers Be a part of this exciting journey with us! About the Role OpusClip is hiring a CX Test Automation Intern: a software-developer-in-test who sits inside the Customer Experience team and turns real customer tickets into automated UI end-to-end tests. You will be the first person in a new lane we call customer-originated requirements: the thousands of support conversations we handle each month are a rich record of how OpusClip actually gets used and where it breaks, and nobody has yet turned that record into a repeatable test battery. This is a 4-month co-op based in Vancouver, starting January 7, 2027, with the option to extend for a further 8 months. The first 4 months hold a bounded, well-defined backlog that is valuable on its own; the extension is a decision we make together, not an assumption. You will work with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex) every day, ship real automation into a real product, and leave with a portfolio of tests that protect paying customers. CX at OpusClip is built as a talent nursery: people who start here move into data, engineering and customer-facing technical roles. This role is designed as one of those on-ramps. This role suits a student or early-career engineer who has already built and shipped something with AI assistance, likes finding the edge cases others miss, and cares about the people on the other side of the product as much as the code. Key Responsibilities Turn customer tickets into automated tests Your core output is a UI end-to-end test battery grounded in real customer reports. You will mine support conversations and bug tickets for the workflows customers actually run and the moments where they fail, reproduce those failures, and write automated tests that catch them before the next customer does. Each test traces back to a ticket, so the battery grows in the direction of real user pain rather than hypothetical coverage. Success here is measured by the share of customer-reported regressions your tests would have caught, and by how much faster CX can confirm a reported issue is real. Map user workflows into testable moments Before a test exists, someone has to break a workflow like "upload a video, get clips, export to TikTok" into its discrete steps, decision points and failure modes, and rank them by how many customers they touch. You will do this mapping with the CX team, who hold the ticket data, and document it so that Product and Engineering can reuse it. Over time this becomes a living map of how OpusClip is used, maintained from the customer side. Work AI-native You will build with Claude Code or Codex as your primary tool: scoping a task, giving the model the right context, breaking the work into steps, reviewing and iterating on the output, and knowing when the first answer is wrong. You will also help the CX team adopt the same habits, sharing patterns and small tools that let non-engineers verify issues and query data on their own. Bridge CX and Engineering You sit in CX but your work lands in Engineering's repositories and CI. You will open pull requests, respond to code review, follow branch and merge conventions, and report flaky or failing tests with clear reproduction steps. When a test exposes a product gap, you will write it up with the customer context, the business impact and a proposed priority, so that the people who own the fix can act on it without a second round of questions. Qualifications and Requirements Hands-on vibe coding experience: Must-have. You have built and shipped something real with AI assistance (a side project, internal tool or script) and can walk through how it was built: what you asked for, what the model got wrong, and how you fixed it. Can read Python and JavaScript/TypeScript: Must-have. You can explain what a short snippet does and spot an obvious bug. You do not need to write either language from scratch. Testing mindset: Must-have. Given a feature such as "upload a video, get clips", you list the happy path, edge cases and failure modes, then rank them by user impact rather than by how easy they are to test. Customer empathy: Must-have. You want to understand what the user was trying to do, not just what broke. You read a ticket and see a person with a deadline, not a bug ID. Clear communication and cross-functional collaboration: Must-have. Your write-ups are short, specific and readable by someone who was not in the room. You ask for review and take feedback without friction. Grasp of business impact: Must-have. You can reason about ROI and opportunity cost: why fixing a bug that hits 2% of paying exports beats one that hits a rarely used free feature, and what it costs to test the wrong thing. Breaks user workflows into discrete moments: Must-have. You can take "upload a video, get clips, post to TikTok" and name each step, each decision the user makes and each place it can go wrong. Curiosity or background in video editing and media: Nice-to-have. You have made, edited or published vid

description: At Upvest, we are on a mission to make investing as easy as spending money . Upvest empowers businesses to offer a wide range of investment products and the best experience in the field of capital market investment and retirement planning. Upvest’s Investment API is easy to integrate so that fintechs and financial institutions can save resources and fully focus on their core business. We are proud to partner with Europe’s leading Fintechs and financial institutions such as DKB, Revolut, N26 and Raisin. Founded in 2017 by Martin Kassing, Upvest now brings together over 270 talented professionals from more than 70 nationalities. Upvest is backed by €280M in total funding from world-class investors, including BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital, and Motive . Our latest €105M funding round in March 2026 - led by Sapphire and Tencent - serves as a massive catalyst for our growth, allowing us to offer premier investment experience. About the role: Germany's private pension system is being rebuilt from the ground up. From 1 January 2027, the Altersvorsorgedepot (AVD) replaces the Riester-Rente as the country's state-subsidised private pension and Upvest is building the operational infrastructure that lets fintechs and banks offer it to millions of savers. Join us as a Working Student in Client Experience and you'll be there before Day 1: helping design the processes, then running them once they go live. This is a rare chance to see a regulated financial product being built from a blank page, rather than inheriting one that already works. What you’ll do: Support our clients: Our partners' support teams field questions from their end-users about subsidies, transfers and payouts. You'll help prepare clear, accurate answers and learn to translate dense regulation into language a customer can act on. Support day-to-day AVD operations: Help run the core processes that keep the product working, e.g. contract registration with the ZfA (Zentrale Zulagenstelle für Altersvermögen), contribution management, the annual bonus application (AZ01), and payment reconciliation. You'll learn how a state-subsidised pension product actually functions behind the interface. Help build the playbooks: As we prepare for launch, we're writing the processes from scratch. You'll help document workflows, build step-by-step guides and error catalogues, and keep them current as the rules and our systems evolve; the foundations the team will scale on. Support error handling and reconciliation: Work through recurring error cases from the ZfA, check that payments and records match, and help spot the patterns behind repeat issues so they can be fixed at the root rather than one at a time. Spot what should be better: You'll see every manual workaround first-hand. We want your view on what's slow, error-prone, or worth automating; and you'll have the room to say so. What you bring: Fluent German communication skills (B2/C1), along with comfortable working proficiency in English This one is a hard requirement rather than a nice-to-have: the regulation, the correspondence with the ZfA, and most of the documentation you'll work with day to day are all in German. You're structured and genuinely precise. In this role, small details carry real consequences for someone's pension, and you're the kind of person who notices when a number doesn't add up. You're curious about rules rather than put off by them. You're willing to read the actual regulation to understand why a process works the way it does. You're comfortable with ambiguity. The product is brand new, so some answers don't exist yet; you'll ask good questions instead of waiting for perfect instructions. You're confident with spreadsheets and AI tooling. Any prior exposure to financial services, operations or a regulated environment is a bonus, but not required. You're available for a minimum of 6 months and based in Berlin. How we Upvest in you: Impact-driven work: We’re building the infrastructure that will power the future of investing in Europe. It’s complex, ambitious, and meaningful. You’ll work with modern technologies and create something entirely new. No legacy systems, no limits. Team celebrations: Participate in company-wide events, such as UpFest, dinners, offsites and our Holiday party, to connect with colleagues and celebrate our achievements. Inclusion : We’re committed to a culture where everyone belongs and thrives. Our Employee Resources Groups foster inclusion and connection, like Upfem for our female Upvengers, or UpVergent supporting neurodivergent Upvengers and allies. Our Values: Make it easy for others. We simplify the complex and act with the best intentions. Own the outcome. We are proactive, fast and confident to get the job done, valuing progress over perfection. Rise to the challenge. We aim high and push the boundaries. We stay curious, learn and celebrate our wins together. Tell the story. We start with the Why to align on purpose. We are transparent and share knowledge to empower and inspire others. Upvest is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Walrus is the leader in B2B payment verification, with clients that include some of the biggest names in investment management. Our DoubleCheck platform combines advanced authentication, proprietary technology, AI, and novel UX to collect and confirm payment details. DoubleCheck has defined a new category: verifying the safe transfer of financial information and assets. Walrus is led by PhD computer scientists and security researchers, with decades of experience in engineering, cybersecurity, and cryptography, and many research accomplishments at Harvard, Stanford, MIT, the University of Chicago, Columbia, UTexas, and NYU. We’re backed by one of the world's leading fintech VC funds, as well as founders and former executives of Twitter, Google Maps, Databricks, and Kayak. The role You will be part of the core team at Walrus, working on our flagship product . You will design, build, and own exciting new modules; examples include payments, reputation, and new kinds of authentication. We are an early-stage company, so you and the team will work together to create standards and culture that will endure for years to come. Of course you’ll get to design and innovate solutions to hard problems, and write a lot of code. But beyond that, as all entrepreneurial software teams do, you’ll be able to design ways of approaching software development. We are looking for people who are thoughtful, not only about software problems, but about how teams work together to solve them, and how people collaborate to build an energizing and supportive workplace. About you You are someone who cares a lot about designing software in a thoughtful way that takes into account bug prevention, testability, and maintainability. You are comfortable with the idea that product design should be data-driven, using evidence rather than opinion. You are: Experienced with tools for testing. You know that the best software developers demonstrate that their code works, rather than dumping it on a QA department. Curious, and have an interest in teaching and learning from your colleagues. A strong written communicator. Graduating in December 2027, anytime 2028, or spring 2029 with an undergraduate degree in computer science, math, physics, or electrical engineering. Optionally We strongly encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all the criteria listed; the description is meant to be indicative, not a precise description of a pigeonhole. You have internship or co-op experience designing, building, and deploying sophisticated web applications. You have experience with modern UI frameworks, web standards, and web development best practices. You have a detailed understanding of the design of data models for use in relational databases. You have used cloud infrastructure to deploy reliable and scalable web applications. You have built authentication flows and/or implemented secure APIs. You have built or used tools for data analysis, performance profiling, and debugging. description:
What we’re building

The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now.

Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water.

The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it

Who we’re looking for

We’re looking for a curious, hands-on engineer who wants to understand how things are built and make the process better. You’ll join our Manufacturing Engineering team in Torrance, working alongside engineers, technicians, supervisors, and quality partners on real production challenges.

With mentorship from a full-time engineer, you’ll own a scoped improvement project from observing the process and collecting data through implementing a solution and measuring the results. You should enjoy spending time on the production floor, listening to the people doing the work, and turning ideas into practical improvements.

Internship Term - June 14–August 20, 2027, onsite at our Torrance headquarters.

What You'll Do

  • Observe production processes and perform time studies to identify bottlenecks, excess motion, rework, and opportunities to reduce build hours.
  • Create and improve work instructions, process flows, and assembly sequences with input from technicians and engineers.
  • Design, prototype, and validate tools, fixtures, and shop aids that improve repeatability, ergonomics, and build quality.
  • Support root-cause investigations into production issues and help implement corrective actions.
  • Partner with design engineering and quality to improve manufacturability and support the introduction of new parts or processes.
  • Use build and quality data to compare performance before and after changes, documenting results and lessons learned.
  • Present your project, results, and recommended next steps to the team at the end of the internship.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Pursuing a degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical or a related engineering discipline.
  • Experience building, assembling, testing, or improving hardware through coursework, a student team, research, an internship, or personal projects.
  • Foundational understanding of engineering drawings, tolerances, and common manufacturing or assembly methods.
  • Basic ability to create or modify parts in a 3D CAD tool.
  • Ability to organize and analyze data using Excel, Google Sheets, or a similar tool.
  • Clear communication, attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to solving problems.
  • Willingness to work hands-on in a production environment, follow safety procedures, and learn from technicians.

Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience with composites, bonding, trimming, finishing, mechanical assembly, or battery manufacturing.
  • Exposure to time studies, standard work, line balancing, lean manufacturing, or continuous improvement.
  • Experience designing fixtures or using machining, 3D printing, or other fabrication methods.
  • Familiarity with NX, Teamcenter, a manufacturing execution system, or digital work instructions.
  • Experience on a student engineering team or in a manufacturing setting.
  • Interest in electric vehicles, boats, and improving how products are built.

At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot.

What we offer

The base pay for this role is $36 per hour. 

Additionally, as an Arc Intern, you'll also get:

  • Boat days – Yes, we actually go out on the water. A lot.
  • Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access
  • Safety support — Reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment, and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe
  • Relocation Assistance
  • Mentorship Opportunities
  • Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite

Our values

We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else:

  • Ownership over both your work and the company’s success
  • Empathy for colleagues and for customers
  • Humility in problem solving and collaboration
  • Pragmatism for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly

We want people who share and embody these values. It is vital that our values align - we’d be happy to elaborate on any or all of these during the interview process.

A Rare Opportunity to Shape the Future of Genomics

Join a team of brilliant, passionate innovators determined to transform healthcare. At BillionToOne, we've built a category-defining, publicly traded company on Nasdaq where transparency fuels trust, collaboration drives breakthroughs, and every contribution moves the needle on our mission to make life-changing diagnostics accessible to all. We don't just aim for incremental improvements; we build products that are 10x better than anything that exists today.

Our scientists, engineers, sales executives, and visionaries are united by an unwavering commitment to changing the standard of care in prenatal and cancer diagnostics. This is where cutting-edge science meets human compassion, and every innovation you contribute helps remove the fear of the unknown from some of life's most critical medical moments.

If you're driven by purpose, energized by innovation, and ready to help shape the future of precision medicine at scale, this is where you belong.

The Research Associate Intern position at BillionToOne is exceptionally rare at the undergraduate or early-career level. At BillionToOne, you will do much more than simply run routine protocols. Your work will shape the development of high-impact molecular diagnostic products that are actively changing patient outcomes in both oncology and prenatal medicine. This is your chance to contribute to building novel molecular tests that help patients from day one.

You will work alongside and be mentored by scientists with interdisciplinary expertise across molecular biology, genomics, bioinformatics, and quantitative modeling. You will have the chance to use cutting-edge molecular techniques, next-generation sequencing, and robotic tools to move assays from research prototypes to commercially available products run at large scale on real patient samples in our clinical lab. Whether your ambition is to grow here at BillionToOne or ultimately pursue graduate studies, this position would be a solid foundation for your scientific career.

The Research Associate intern is an on-site position in our Menlo Park, CA office.

Candidates who expect to graduate before Fall 2027 or who have already graduated are encouraged to apply to our full-time Research Associate position.

Who We’re Looking For:

  • Strong statistical and quantitative skills: You think rigorously about data. You understand the difference between signal and noise, appreciate the importance of statistical power, and bring quantitative reasoning to every problem.
  • Meticulous attention to experimental detail: You understand that the quality of an experiment determines what we can learn from it. You keep rigorous records, design careful controls, and take pride in work that others can rely on and build upon.
  • Ambition to make a difference now: You aren’t here to punch the clock. You want to understand why things work, push the boundaries of what’s known, and do what it takes to see your contributions show up in products that help real patients.
  • Excellent communication in a fast-paced, collaborative environment: We move quickly and we move together. You share findings clearly and proactively, ask questions early rather than late, and work seamlessly across scientists, engineers, and cross-functional teams to keep projects moving.

Responsibilities:

  • Design, execute, and troubleshoot experiments and assays under the guidance of Senior Scientists
  • Learn analytical and computational methodologies to analyze results under the guidance of Senior Scientists
  • Present scientific findings both verbally at group meetings and via internal written reports
  • Document experimental details and results

Qualifications:

  • Must be enrolled in an undergraduate or master’s degree program during Fall 2027
  • Anticipated BS or MS in Bioengineering, Molecular and Cell Biology, Microbiology, Biophysics, Biochemistry, or related field
  • Independent research experience
  • An ability to quickly learn mathematical, analytical, and experimental concepts
  • High mathematical and statistical aptitude (e.g., you find GRE math section to be extremely easy)
  • Great attention to detail

Nice-To-Haves:

  • Experience with standard molecular biology techniques relating to DNA such as PCR
  • Experience in a cell-free DNA setting
  • Experience with next-generation sequencing library preparation
  • Experience with computational analysis in R, Python, or other programming language

Benefits And Perks:

  • Open, transparent culture that includes weekly Town Hall meetings
  • The ability to indirectly or directly change the lives of hundreds of thousand patients
  • Free daily on-site lunches provided from top eateries

For this position, the base pay rate is $25 per hour.

At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Team

Celonis Services is the delivery engine of our Celonis Customer Organization, responsible for turning the Celonis platform into measurable, business-critical outcomes for our customers. In the AI era, our role has elevated: as AI agents like our own Apollo take on more of the technical build, our people focus on the work that drives real impact — understanding our customers' business-critical problems, designing the solutions that solve them, and quantifying the value delivered. Our team pairs deep domain and industry expertise with serious platform mastery and AI-augmented delivery, directing agentic systems while owning the judgment, architecture, and customer relationships that AI cannot replace. We deliver faster and smarter than ever, and we own the outcome: solution go-live, solution adoption, initial value realization support and the long-term success of our customers.

The Role

As an intern, you will have the unique opportunity to learn and grow through hands-on experiences. Your role will involve utilizing our cutting-edge AI deployment tools to develop innovative solutions for our customers, together with more experienced Deployment Engineers.

This is not a traditional engineering role where you build everything manually. You will be introduced to AI-augmented and business-focused software delivery: helping specify what needs to be built, learning to direct AI agents to execute, and assisting in validating the results. Participation in team meetings and workshops will offer valuable insights into the decision-making process within the company.

The Work You’ll Do

Initiate and Connect

  • Conduct customer-facing sessions with experienced Deployment Engineers to discuss ongoing projects, translate strategic objectives into use cases, and receive guidance on best practices.
  • Assist in gathering and organizing relevant data from various sources, ensuring data accuracy and consistency for analysis.

Build

  • Learn to direct AI deployment agents (like Apollo) to build data models, process analyses, KPIs, and dashboards by helping to write clear specifications.
  • Conduct exploratory data analysis, utilizing Celonis and other tools to uncover trends, process inefficiencies, and root causes.
  • Assist in defining the initial solution design blueprint and configuring operational solutions across the platform.

Value & Rollout

  • Support the validation of AI-generated outputs for accuracy and business relevance alongside senior team members.
  • Help develop and maintain KPIs to track the success of project initiatives and quantify business impact.
  • Assist in documenting solution design decisions and configurations for future reference and customer handover.

What Makes This Role Different in the AI Era

  • You will learn to work with AI agents as your primary tools, focusing on validating and refining their output rather than writing every line of code manually.
  • You will develop foundational specification and context engineering skills to help translate business needs into precise AI instructions.
  • As you navigate a fast-paced environment, you will learn how to adapt quickly to changes and new approaches as AI capabilities evolve.

The Qualifications You Need

  • Student of Technology Management, Business (-Informatics), Computer Science, Engineering, Economics, or a comparable degree program with outstanding performance.
  • Know-how in Business Intelligence, data analytics, and a foundational understanding of enterprise business processes.
  • Experience in programming and working with databases; knowledge in SQL, Python, or related coding- and/or database query languages.
  • Curiosity and basic familiarity with AI-assisted development tools, coupled with an eagerness to learn prompt/context engineering.
  • Interest in working with customers, along with awesome presentation and communication skills.
  • Ability to demonstrate initiative, work independently, and think outside of the box.
  • Fluent in English and German (any additional language is a plus).
  • At least 5 months of full-time availability.

What Celonis can offer you:

  • Pioneer Innovation: Work with the global leader in Process Mining and the Process Intelligence Graph to shape the future of AI-driven business operations.
  • Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time "Celonaut" is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.

description:
Chicago Trading Company (CTC) is a premier proprietary trading firm specializing in options market making.  Our collaborative culture fuels innovation in quantitative research, systematic trading strategies, and cutting-edge trading technology.  For over three decades CTC has provided critical liquidity across derivatives exchanges worldwide - making them fairer, more transparent, and more efficient.

We strive to be the most innovative firm in the industry today, tomorrow, and long into the future while upholding ethical excellence. We believe that CTC makes a positive impact on the markets, the lives of our employees, and all the communities to which we belong. Started in 1995 by a team of forward-thinking Traders, we are proud to call ourselves an industry leader that keeps making markets and each other better.

We are currently seeking an Accounting Intern to join Chicago Trading Company (CTC)! As an Accounting Intern, you will be challenged to learn and adapt in a fast-paced environment and will play a role in the firm's daily financial operations.  

What you'll do 

You will focus on a mix of daily operational accounting tasks as well as on internship-specific project work tailored to match CTC initiatives with your future career goals. As part of the Summer Associate cohort, you will also have the opportunity to learn from and network with Quant Trading Interns and Software Engineering Interns. 

Operational Accounting 

  • Assist with the posting and reconciling of daily financial activity in the GL 
  • Review daily cash activity and ensure transactions are accurately recorded 
  • Participate in the month-end close process, including the analysis of accruals, fixed assets, and prepaid transactions  
  • Prepare variance analysis for specific CTC legal entities and/or PnL groups 

 

Internship-Specific Projects 

  • 2-6 week projects defined at the start of the internship, designed to pair intern interests with Accounting team initiatives.

title: Software Engineer Intern

description:
Who we are 

CloudKitchens helps restaurateurs around the world succeed in online food delivery - our goal is to make food more affordable, higher quality and convenient for everyone. 

We take underutilized properties and transform them into smart kitchens so they can better serve restaurateurs, customers and the neighborhoods they’re in. Every time we launch a new facility we create jobs in that neighborhood, and we’re proud to provide a wide range of cuisines and options for healthy food at an affordable price.

We're changing the game for restaurateurs whether they’re entrepreneurs opening their first restaurant all the way through to your favorite global quick-service restaurant chains.  

 

What you’ll do

Sales execution and deal support

  • Support Account Executives in day-to-day sales execution pipeline management, and opportunity follow-up
  • Conduct prospect research prior to sales calls (company context, decision-makers, recent news)
  • Own the drafting and updating of commercial contracts, proposals and deal documentation
  • Maintain and update sales systems and internal tools to ensure smooth deal execution

Inbound qualification (SDR scope)

  • Qualify inbound leads (website, email, referrals) using defined qualification criteria
  • Conduct first-level discovery calls to assess fit, urgency and decision-making structure
  • Route qualified opportunities to Account Executives with clear context, notes and next steps
  • Maintain accurate CRM records and update lead statuses throughout the qualification process.
  • Ensure prompt follow-up on inbound leads to maximize engagement and conversion opportunities.

Research and targeting

  • Build and enrich target account and prospect lists for Mid-Market and Enterprise accounts
  • Identify key decision-makers and relevant stakeholders
  • Conduct market and competitor research to support outbound strategies

Commercial communication (LinkedIn)

  • Help draft and schedule sales-oriented LinkedIn posts (market insights, deal announcements, thought leadership)
  • Monitor engagement and contribute to improving content performance

Prospection and outreach support

  • Support outbound campaigns (email sequences, follow-ups, automation workflows)
  • Help structure and automate repetitive outreach tasks to improve sales efficiency

CRM and sales operations

  • Ensure CRM hygiene (data accuracy, pipeline updates, process adherence)
  • Support the implementation and adoption of new sales processes and workflows

 

What we’re looking for

  • Excellent English skills (you’ll be working in Shakespeare’s language 50% of the time!)
  • Organized, meticulous, and proactive, combining enthusiasm, a positive attitude, and unwavering motivation on a daily basis
  • Highly creative, resourceful, and data-driven with a strong analytical mindset; comfortable with rapid iteration and quickly pivoting strategies
  • Enjoys challenges and motivated to work in a fast-growing company
  • Excellent communication skills: loves meeting new people and engaging with multiple stakeholders every day
  • Familiarity with CRM tools (e.g., Salesforce) is a plus!
  • Interest in sales technology, data analysis and workflow automation is a plus!

 

Why join us 

  • Demand for online food delivery is growing really fast! In the last 5 years, just in the US, the overall market has expanded 10X from $10B to $100B, and could expand to $500bn- $1T by 2030.
  • Changing the restaurant industry: You’ll be part of a team that helps restaurants succeed in online food delivery. 
  • Collaborative environment: You will receive support and guidance from experienced colleagues and managers, helping you to learn, grow and achieve your goals, and you’ll work closely with other teams to ensure our customer’s success.

 

What else you need to know 

This role is based in our Paris office location. As a company driven by innovation and continuous change, close collaboration is essential. We’re constantly reimagining our industry, creating new products, and refining our processes, and we do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week. 

  • Duration: 6 months
  • Start date: January, 2027
  • Location: Paris, France (office-based)
  • Internship agreement: Required
  • Salary: €1,400 / month + Swile + 50% Navigo reimbursement

 

Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?

description:
About the Team

DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better 

About the Role

As a Mechanical Engineering Intern, you will work on all aspects of the mechanical design process, including design, analysis, prototyping, and validation of components and systems for DoorDash's next-generation autonomous delivery vehicle.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Design detailed components and sub-assemblies for a high-profile delivery robot, with the support of your mentor, manager, and team members.
  • Build production-quality 3D CAD models and drawings, and present your work in cross-functional design reviews.
  • Collaborate with electrical, systems, and manufacturing engineers to make sure your designs integrate cleanly and can be manufactured, assembled, and serviced at fleet scale.
  • Learn how to validate designs through prototype builds, bench testing, and tolerance and structural analysis, and act on feedback

We’re excited about you because…

  • You are pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering or a related field (such as Mechatronics, Robotics, Aerospace, or Automotive Engineering), have no more than 2 years of full-time work experience, and are available for a May or June 2027 start date (internships are only hosted during the summer).
  • You have hands-on experience with 3D CAD (such as NX, SolidWorks, or CATIA), preferably NX.
  • You have a solid grasp of engineering fundamentals and use first principles, calculations, simulation, and test data to support design decisions.
  • You have shown interest in mechanical design through coursework, team projects (such as Formula SAE or robotics clubs), or personal builds.
  • You can work independently on assigned design tasks and you want to learn how products are designed, built, and operated at scale.

Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis

Compensation

Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location. 

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

See below for paid time off details:

  • For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year.
  • For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week).
The national base pay range for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado.
$89,100—$131,000 USD

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

description:
About Us

DriveWealth is on a mission to make investing easier. We believe that everyone should have the ability to control their financial future, and that access to financial markets should not be limited by geography, wealth, or legacy systems. We are a global B2B financial technology organization dedicated to democratizing access to financial independence around the world. Our mission is realized through an API-based platform, empowering our partners to offer seamless investing and trading experiences to clients worldwide, all from their mobile devices. Our technology provides partners with a modern, extensible toolkit, enabling traditional investment workflows and innovative techniques like fractional share ownership. DriveWealth has evolved into a global platform offering trading of US equities, mutual funds, ETFs, fixed income, and options.

There’s never been a better time to build a category-defining business and there has rarely been a team better positioned for this opportunity. Our culture blends the pace and agility of a fintech start-up with the impact, stability, and discipline of Wall Street. We encourage creativity and experimentation while ensuring institutional-grade execution and regulatory compliance in everything we do. Join us and help build the future of global investing!

Interested to learn more about our AI CAP Program? We will have our in-person Open House at our CHI office office on November 23rd (RSVP here: https://partiful.com/e/53eY3haJAUxm6leyFo5v)

About the Role

We are seeking an AI Product intern who will work on real AI agentic automation problems, designing, prototyping, and developing AI-powered agents to help the business and engineers achieve faster, smarter work. You will collaborate directly with senior engineers and architects, receiving mentorship and design reviews, and gaining exposure to modern GenAI patterns, including agent orchestration, tool-calling, retrieval, and evaluation, within an enterprise and fast-paced fintech environment.

AI tools change every quarter. Your project will use the best models, agent frameworks, and protocols available in summer 2027. You will work on current practice, not today's stack.

Launch your career developing real, impactful AI solutions in the lightning-fast world of fintech!

Program Details
Our summer program will be 10-12 weeks from May - August 2027 with the expectation of being in the office 3-4 days per week, as determined by the sponsor. Compensation will be set at an hourly rate of $35-40 per hour. Top performing associates may have the opportunity to be considered for full-time roles at DriveWealth at the conclusion of the program, based on performance and team needs. Must have a graduation date in 2027 or 2028 .

What You’ll Do

  • Design, prototype, and develop agentic AI workflows that automate or augment business or engineering tasks (for example, analysis, triage, documentation, and knowledge synthesis)
  • Build internal tools or proof-of-concept systems that combine LLMs, APIs, and automation frameworks into end-to-end agentic solutions
  • Experiment with different agent architectures (single-agent vs. multi-agent, planner/executor patterns, human-in-the-loop workflows) and document tradeoffs
  • Apply best practices when building AI-driven automation
  • Evaluate agent behavior for reliability, correctness, and failure modes, and propose improvements
  • Clearly document designs, experiments, and lessons learned so work can be reused or extended by the team
  • Demo your work directly to customers and the leadership team

What You’ll Need

  • Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related technical field
  • Experience programming in Python (for automation, prototyping, and scripting) and SQL
  • Familiarity with APIs, JSON, and basic service integration
  • Foundational understanding of large language models and how they are used in applications (prompting, tool use, retrieval, etc.)
  • Strong curiosity and willingness to explore new, rapidly evolving technologies
  • A growth mindset: you ask questions and enjoy experimenting and iterating
  • Systems thinking: able to reason about workflows, edge cases, and unintended consequences
  • Clear written and verbal communication, especially when explaining technical ideas to non-engineers
  • Ownership mindset: you take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks
  • Ability to accept feedback and iterate quickly


Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. DriveWealth is unable to sponsor an employment Visa at this time.

Working at DriveWealth

We do our best work when we're in the same room. To maintain the speed our partners expect, our New York, Chicago, and Lithuania teams work in office on a hybrid schedule. We've found that being physically side-by-side is the only way to solve complex problems in real-time and stay truly accountable to the products we ship. When you're here, you're working directly with the people making the decisions.

description:
Actuarial internship for summer of 2027.

Horace Mann Educators Corporation offers insurance and financial products to educators and those who serve the public. We’re motivated by the fact that educators take care of our children’s future, and we believe they deserve someone to look after theirs. We help educators identify their financial goals and develop plans to achieve them. Our tailored offerings include special rates and benefits for educators, as well as the insurance we’re known for in order to help protect what they have today and the financial products to help prepare them for their futures.

The Role

Our Life and Retirement (L&R) Actuarial team is seeking an L&R Actuarial Intern, who will gain hands-on experience in the development, modeling, and financial analysis of life insurance and retirement / annuity products tailored for educators.  Under direct supervision from various senior members of the team, you will also gain exposure to assumption setting, risk assessment, and regulatory compliance within the insurance industry. It's a great opportunity to apply your quantitative skills and learn how actuarial principles are applied in real-world scenarios to build a foundation for a successful actuarial career.

Our ideal candidate will have the ability to travel to our Springfield, IL offices weekly, per the hybrid work schedule.

The Day-to-Day

  • Product Pricing & Modeling: Assist in building, maintaining, and running actuarial projection models (such MG-ALFA or Excel-based tools) to evaluate the profitability of life and annuity products.
  • Profitability Analysis: Help prepare profit summaries, sensitivity testing, and risk analysis for senior audiences. 
  • Assumption Setting: Work with key pricing assumptions such as mortality, lapse rates, and expenses to gain an understanding for the impact they have on product profitability.  Gain exposure to experience data as a way to learn how assumptions are developed.
  • Competitive Analysis: Review analysis containing competitor product pricing, design, and features to help position Horace Mann products in line with company goals.  Gain an understanding of the various insurance products offered by Horace Mann and their specific actuarial considerations.
  • Process Optimization: Identify opportunities to improve or automate existing spreadsheets to drive higher team efficiency.
  • Team Building: Actively participate in various department and project-focused meetings, engage and contribute ideas, and gain exposure to cross-functional collaboration.

Role Requirements

  • Academic Background: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in actuarial science, finance, economics, statistics, mathematics, business, or related field.
  • Actuarial Exams: A minimum of one (1) Actuarial exam through either the Society of Actuaries (SOA) or the Casualty Actuary Society (CAS) must be completed.

Technical & Soft Skills

  • Technical Proficiency: Expertise in Microsoft Excel (including pivot tables and advanced functions). Exposure to programming languages (SQL, Python, R, or VBA) or dedicated actuarial software is a plus.
  • Analytical Thinking: Exceptional abilities in the analytical space to analyze data, interpret trends, and make sound recommendations.
  • Communication: Compelling written and verbal communication skills are essential for presenting findings, collaborating with team members, and explaining complex concepts to stakeholders.
  • Collaboration: A proactive team member who is eager to learn, adapt to feedback, and manage multiple project deadlines efficiently.
  • Time Management: Detail-oriented and organized to prioritize work and time effectively.
  • Growth Mindset: Being open to growth and learning new skills is an essential piece of the mentality we cultivate in cohesion with our customers - America’s Educators!

 

Pay Range: $26/hour.  Salary is commensurate to experience, location, etc.

HP IQ's Hardware Design team is responsible for materializing product vision into manufacturable hardware systems. The position offers the opportunity to own the mechanical and systems integration challenges that transform concepts into shipping products.

What You Might Do

  • Collaborate with Industrial Design to translate product vision into mechanical design, enclosure layout, and form factor feasibility
  • Integrate multiple subsystems (microphone, speaker, antenna, battery, PCB, sensors, buttons) into a cohesive hardware architecture

  • Portfolio demonstrating complete hardware projects from design through prototype or production
  • Experience with assembly process design, datuming, and fixturing
  • Familiarity with cross-functional product development from concept through production ramp
