Company Overview

ID.me is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with ID.me once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 175 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with ID.me at 22 federal agencies, 50 state government agencies, and more than 100 healthcare organizations. Over 600 consumer brands use ID.me to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. ID.me’s technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. ID.me is committed to “No Identity Left Behind” to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit https://network.id.me/.

ID.me is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings.

At ID.me, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. However, during the interview process, we want to understand your individual skills and experiences. Therefore, we have guidelines on how AI can be appropriately used during your application and interviews which can be found here.

Role Overview 

ID.me is looking for an Analytics Engineer Intern to help us put AI to work across our data organization. You are a curious builder who loves turning data into answers, and you’re ready to use AI to put those answers in the hands of the teams who rely on them every day.

As an intern, you'll build conversational analytics chatbots, automate data pipelines, and create detection agents that help us get more from our data and improve the member experience.

Location: Mountain View, California- onsite in office five days a week 

What You'll Work On

As an intern, you will own a focused set of AI enablement projects, working alongside analytics engineers, data analysts, and data engineers.

  • Conversational analytics chatbots: Build chatbots that let teams ask questions of our data in plain language and get trusted answers.
  • Data pipeline automation: Use AI-assisted tooling to automate and streamline parts of our data pipelines.
  • Detection agents: Design agents that monitor data and flag anomalies, quality issues, and unusual patterns.
  • Data architecture and domain-driven design: Explore how AI can improve our data models, documentation, and overall architecture.

Responsibilities

  • Build and iterate on chatbot prototypes that support conversational analytics on top of Snowflake and dbt models
  • Automate data pipeline tasks such as testing, documentation, and monitoring using AI tools
  • Develop detection agents that surface data quality problems and anomalies
  • Apply domain-driven design principles to help improve data models, metric definitions, and metadata
  • Partner with analysts, engineers, and data scientists to understand needs and gather feedback
  • Document your work and present results and learnings to the team at the end of the internship

Basic Qualifications

  • College junior with an expected graduation year of 2028, currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Data Analytics, Statistics, Math, or a related quantitative field. Students with a software engineering background who want to build a career in data are encouraged to apply.
  • Interest in AI and large language models, including prompting and building simple applications on top of them
  • Basic understanding of data modeling and data warehousing concepts

What You'll Gain

  • Hands-on experience building AI-powered analytics tools on a modern data stack
  • Mentorship from experienced analytics engineers
  • A real project with visible impact on how ID.me uses its data
  • Exposure to data architecture, domain-driven design, and data governance in practice
  • A portfolio-ready project to present to the team at the end of the internship

Our Culture

At ID.me, we believe that an in-office culture fosters professional growth and development, mentorship, collaboration, and accelerated innovation. This position will be in-office based at our Mountain View, CA location. Working in an office together allows our culture to thrive and our team members to establish real connections with their coworkers and the opportunity for lifelong friendships. Our work is critical to protecting online identity and we're confident that working together is how we'll change the world.

At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets.

Position Summary: 

The Manufacturing Engineering Co-Op will support the development and optimization of manufacturing processes and systems in a hands-on, fast-paced production environment. Over the course of this 12-week program, the co-op will work closely with experienced engineers and cross-functional teams to contribute to process improvement, data analysis, documentation development, and implementation of Lean and Industry 4.0 initiatives. This is a great opportunity for an aspiring engineer to gain real-world experience and apply classroom knowledge to practical challenges in modern manufacturing. 

 

This position requires 100% onsite work at our Jacksonville, FL office. Relocation support may be available to eligible interns based on established criteria, including school location and distance from the assigned worksite.

 

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Assist with time studies, process mapping, and data collection to support improvement of manufacturing workflows. 
  • Participate in the development or update of standard work instructions, process documentation, and visual aids. 
  • Support small-scale improvement projects related to process optimization, layout redesign, or material flow. 
  • Collaborate with manufacturing, quality, and engineering teams to identify opportunities for waste reduction and productivity improvement. 
  • Assist in preparing presentations and reports to communicate findings and recommendations to stakeholders. 
  • Observe and document current manufacturing processes to gain exposure to Lean Manufacturing principles and practices. 
  • Contribute to brainstorming sessions, kaizen events, or root cause investigations as appropriate. 
  • Participate in safety and quality audits or checklists to understand compliance requirements in a production environment. 
  • Gain exposure to CAD software, ERP systems, and/or basic automation tools under guidance. 
  • Complete and present an end-of-term report to the manufacturing leadership.

 

Qualifications: 

  • Pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field. 
  • Basic understanding of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or process improvement concepts (coursework or project experience is a plus). 
  • Familiarity with engineering tools such as Excel, CAD software, or data analysis programs is preferred. 
  • Strong attention to detail, willingness to learn, and ability to work collaboratively in a team setting. 
  • Excellent communication skills and a proactive attitude toward problem-solving. 

 

 

Why Join IEM

At IEM, you’ll join a team that powers some of the world’s most ambitious projects. We’re engineers, makers, and problem-solvers who thrive on tackling complex challenges and delivering solutions that keep industries moving forward. If you’re driven, collaborative, and ready to make an impact, we’d love to hear from you. Your creativity and passion can help us achieve great things—come be part of the journey.

Learn more about IEM at https://www.iemfg.com

We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support our employees' well-being, growth, and long-term success. View a snapshot of our benefits at https://www.iemfg.com/careers

We are always looking for amazing talent who can contribute to our growth and deliver results! Geotab is seeking a Data Governance & Operations Data Analyst Intern to help keep the company's most important data accurate, trusted and easy to use. You will work with large datasets to find patterns, check quality and answer business questions. If you love technology, and are keen to join an industry leader, we would love to hear from you!

What you'll do:

The Global Data Operations & Governance (GDOG) team owns the certified metrics, scheduled data pipelines and data standards that teams across Geotab rely on. As an intern you will help build, check and maintain those data assets using SQL and statistical tools. On a typical day you will work closely with your manager and a team member who guides your focus area, alongside the other interns on the team and partner teams across the business. The successful candidate is an analytical problem solver who enjoys diving into data, is excited about investigations, can multi-task, and can credibly interface between technical teams and others.

The opportunity:

  • 12-month work-term beginning January 2027.
  • Full-time, paid internship: Monday - Friday, 37.5hrs/week.
  • Your first week at Geotab begins with 'GEO Launch' - a one-week Employee Orientation. Click here to learn more!
  • Learn more about the Geotab Campus Program here.
  • This posting is for an existing vacancy.

How you'll make an impact:

  • Work with the GDOG team and partner teams (such as Revenue Operations, Finance and Marketing) to deliver accurate, consistent data.
  • Use AI coding assistants (such as Claude Code or Codex) every day to write and review SQL and Python, build reports, automate data quality checks and pipeline monitoring, and draft documentation, then check and own what they produce.
  • Check data quality at every stage: sourcing, collection, normalization and transformation. Reconcile numbers between systems and explain any gaps.
  • Help monitor scheduled data pipelines, investigate failures and document the cause and fix.

From our global network of research and development sites, we are committed to discovering and developing safe, effective, and cutting-edge therapies for patients worldwide.

  • Microsoft office suite.

Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is looking for a hands-on engineering co-op to help build and test the automated systems that run our laboratory workflows. Reporting to a senior manager on the Automated Systems Engineering team and paired with a day-to-day mentor, you will work alongside engineers and scientists on real workcells that are being deployed.

This is a lab-floor role. You will spend your time integrating instruments and troubleshooting systems that run live experiments. By the end of the co-op you should own a meaningful piece of a system and understand how scientific goals turn into working hardware.

Along the way you will see how scientific objectives become scoped technical requirements, how science, hardware, controls, and software teams coordinate interfaces on a shared system, and how automated experiments generate the structured, high-quality data that feeds AI-driven experimental design. You will also get hands-on time with emerging lab technology, including machine vision, advanced sensors, and automated scheduling software.

What You'll Be Building

  • Support cross-functional requirements gathering and project documentation using established team templates and execution guidelines.
  • Assist in converting manual scientific protocols into automation concept designs through process mapping, step timing, and identification of automation candidates.
  • Research new instruments and technologies, and help evaluate them for physical integration capability and fit with scientific workflows.
  • Contribute to concept design documentation, system architecture diagrams, and interface definitions for workcell- and instrument-level projects.
  • Maintain and update the federated factory layout model, producing layout drawings and 3D models that account for robotics envelopes, human ergonomics, and hazard zones.
  • Support feasibility assessments for proposed automation opportunities and help document lab automation best practices and lessons learned.

  • Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program in Biomedical, Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, Robotics, or Chemical Engineering, Bioengineering, or a related field

  • Working knowledge of Python through coursework, projects, or prior internships

description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is hiring a co-op to join the Materials Science team within the Autonomous Science Platform. You will characterize electrodeposited metal films and develop the measurement methods that make those results repeatable. Deposition is handled by other scientists on the team; your focus is measurement, method development, and data quality.

The role spans electrical, surface, structural, and mechanical techniques: four-point probe for sheet resistance and resistivity, laser confocal metrology for thickness, step height, and roughness, XRD and EBSD for phase, texture, and grain structure, and hardness testing for mechanical properties. Much of the work is standing these methods up: defining sample prep, acquisition settings, and acceptance criteria so results hold across operators and sample batches.

You will work alongside scientists and engineers in a lab built for high-throughput, automated experimentation, and your protocols will feed directly into how these measurements get scaled.

What You'll Be Building

  • Develop sample prep and measurement protocols for general characterization tools on electrodeposited films: four-point probe, hardness testing, and SEM/EBSD.
  • Prepare samples for SEM and EBSD (mounting, polishing, surface cleanup)
  • Run four-point probe, laser confocal metrology, and hardness measurements
  • Analyze XRD data (phase ID, texture, peak shift, crystallite size) and EBSD data (grain size, orientation, texture)
  • Validate measurement repeatability and establish data quality criteria
  • Analyze and visualize characterization data, then document methods and failure modes

  • Pursuing a bachelor's, master's, or PhD in Materials Science, Physics, Chemistry, Mechanical/Chemical Engineering, or a related field
  • Hands-on experience operating materials characterization instruments in a lab

Your Impact at LILA

As a Co-Op on the Production Robotics team at Lila Sciences, you will help build the algorithms and software that let our robots know where they are and what they are looking at, so they can run scientific workflows reliably inside the AI Science Factories (AISFs). The team develops the state estimation, perception, and testing infrastructure that general-purpose robotic skills depend on.

Your work will sit at the intersection of estimation, computer vision, and robotics software. You will help improve how our mobile bases estimate their position and motion, develop camera-based detection and localization of AprilTags and lab instruments, and strengthen the simulation-based testing and CI that validate changes before they reach hardware. Expect a mix of writing production-quality software, applying math to real sensor data, and debugging real-world behavior on physical robots.

You will work alongside robotics engineers, AI researchers, and software engineers, with day-to-day support from the Production Robotics team. The output is software that runs in production lab environments and directly accelerates the rate at which Lila can run experiments.

What You'll Be Building

  • Fuse multi-sensor data to improve mobile base state estimation
  • Build camera-based AprilTag and instrument detection and localization for robot manipulation and navigation
  • Develop new robot capabilities in ROS 2 (Jazzy)
  • Expand simulation-based tests and CI pipelines so changes are validated before deployment on hardware
  • Evaluate estimation and perception performance on real robot data and contribute fixes back to the codebase
  • Ship production code alongside robotics, software, and AI engineers
  • Document algorithms, test approaches, and integration patterns for the rest of the team

What You'll Need to Succeed

  • In-progress Master's (preferred) or strong senior-year Bachelor's in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, with a controls/estimation leaning
  • Proficiency in Python and/or C++, with coursework or project experience writing well-tested code

  • Comfort with Git and Linux development environments

Parallel Systems is pioneering autonomous battery-electric rail vehicles designed to transform freight transportation by shifting portions of the $900 billion U.S. trucking industry onto rail. Our innovative technology offers cleaner, safer, and more efficient logistics solutions. Join our dynamic team and help shape a smarter, greener future for global freight.

Software Engineering Interns

Parallel Systems is seeking Software Engineering Interns to help build the software that runs our vehicles and the platform behind our fleet. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to ship real work. Your code will run on prototype vehicles, on test benches, or in the services and tools our team and operators rely on every day.

Interns are placed on a vehicle software or backend/full-stack project based on their background and team priorities. You will own a scoped project from requirements through delivery, work closely with a mentor, and see your work tested on real hardware or used by real users.

The right person is curious beyond their own layer. Whether you are writing firmware, building a service, or shipping an internal tool, you will learn how software, hardware, and vehicle data fit together, and you will be comfortable debugging across those boundaries.

What You Will Work On

  • Weeks 8-10: Supporting build and testing with the engineering team, user feedback sessions, and iteration on scope

Progress will be tracked through weekly check-ins with your mentor, spec and design reviews, and feedback from engineering, operations, and users.

  • Strong written communication, including the ability to write clear, concise specs and documents

Whether your background leans toward robotics (planning, control, kinematics) or machine learning (perception, reinforcement learning, deep learning), we’ll match you with a project that fits your strengths — and you’ll see your code run on live robotic cells doing real work. Every intern owns a scoped, production-relevant project from design through testing on real hardware, then presents results to the team at the end of the summer. Depending on your interests, your project could include:

  • Robotics: motion and trajectory planning, inverse kinematics and reachability, real-time control and feedback loops, visual servoing, or localization and navigation for mobile platforms.

description:
About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

About the Role: 

We are seeking a talented and motivated Chargeback Operations Intern who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement.

As a Chargeback Operations Intern, you will be responsible for analyzing and responding to card and ACH disputes filed against Sezzle. Working closely with our fraud/risk team and our customer disputes team, you will navigate issues on a case by case basis to determine the best course of action to help our customers get unstuck. Analysts will also make recommendations to our management on how to improve and scale our processes. 

We are looking for a teammate who can work full-time Monday through Friday between 9:00 am - 5:30 pm - Central Time. This will be a paid internship.

What You'll Do:

  • Investigate disputed credit card, debit card, and ACH transactions and take suitable action to resolve those disputes within the allowed timeframes.
  • Work cross functionally with relevant departments (fraud, disputes) to determine next steps on a case to case basis.
  • Investigate individual transactions using internal policies and review methodologies to identify patterns or trends.
  • Understand our systems and tools; investigate account patterns through data analysis.
  • Collaborate with analysts, operations specialists, data scientists and engineering to improve our loss prevention mechanisms, processes and tools.
  • Learn and maintain strong domain knowledge of the world of fraud including prevention techniques and technologies.
  • Maintain or exceed established service level agreements (SLAs) for timely resolution of queued cases to minimize potential losses.
  • Handle escalations from internal and external stakeholders in a professional and efficient manner.
  • Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication.

What We Look For:

  • Experience in analyzing data and comfortable making impactful decisions in a fast-paced and sometimes ambiguous environment
  • Attention to detail and ability to multitask
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills
  • Strong business judgment and communication skills
  • Ability to self-start and work with minimal supervision after training

About You:

  • You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You’re not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things
  • You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
  • You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
  • You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome:

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire. 

Compensation: The salary for the Chargeback Operations Intern is $800 USD monthly as an independent contractor.

#Full-time 

Pay Range
$800—$800 USD

At SK Hynix Memory Solution, we're at the forefront of semiconductor innovation, developing advanced memory solutions that power everything from smartphones to data centers. As a global leader in DRAM and NAND flash technologies, we drive the evolution of advancing mobile technology, empowering cloud computing, and pioneering future technologies. Our cutting-edge memory technologies are essential in today's most advanced electronic devices and IT infrastructure, enabling enhanced performance and user experiences across the digital landscape.

We're looking for innovative minds to join our mission of shaping the future of technology. At SK Hynix Memory, you'll be part of a team that's pioneering breakthrough memory solutions while maintaining a strong commitment to sustainability. We're not just adapting to technological change – we're driving it, with significant investments in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and eco-friendly solutions and operational practices. As we continue to expand our market presence and push the boundaries of what's possible in semiconductor technology, we invite you to be part of our journey to creating the next generation of memory solutions that will define the future of computing.

 

Internship Duration: 6 months

Hours: 40 hours per week

Start Date: Immediately (November 2026/December 2026) 

Location: San Jose

 

About The Role

You will join the System on Chip (SoC) Design Team at SK hynix memory solutions America, a group dedicated to delivering best-in-class controllers for high-performance SSDs. This team spans the full design cycle—from micro-architecture and RTL design to timing closure and tapeout readiness—enabling next-generation enterprise and AI data center storage solutions.

 

Responsibilities

  • RTL design (Verilog/SystemVerilog) for IP based on existing module or new specifications.
  • Collaborate, create clear documentation and communication with Design Verification, Silicon Validation, and Firmware teams to ensure design quality.

 

Minimum Qualifications

  • Education: Currently enrolled in BS/MS/PhD program in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field.
  • Proficiency in logic design and micro-architecture; RTL coding in Verilog and/or SystemVerilog language.

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced Education: Master’s or PhD in Electrical Engineering with working experiences.
  • Experience or coursework in digital logic design, verification methodologies, and protocols (AMBA, PCIe, NAND, DDR)
  • Scripting skills (Python, Perl, TCL) and Linux command-line experiences
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills
  • Proficiency in AI tool to generate synthesizable and functional RTL code

COMPENSATION: $35/hr - $45/hr

description:
Stratolaunch accelerates the development of next-generation aerospace and defense technologies through reusable hypersonic flight testing. Our autonomous, air-launched Talon-A vehicles provide access to operationally realistic flight environments at speeds exceeding Mach 5, delivering critical data that helps customers validate system performance and advance technologies toward deployment. Our team brings together expertise in engineering, manufacturing, and flight operations to solve complex challenges and advance capabilities essential to national security.

Application window closes 11/7/26

Stratolaunch is seeking a detail-orientated and driven Supply Chain Intern to support our operations team. This role offers hands-on experience in a fast-paced environment, with exposure to procurement, aircraft parts logistics, inventory control, and vendor coordination critical to maintaining operational readiness.

 

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

 

Procurement

  • Assist with creating and processing purchase requisitions and purchase orders for production materials, components, tooling, and indirect supplies.
  • Support buyers in obtaining supplier quotes, confirming lead times, and tracking order status.
  • Help maintain accurate purchasing records, pricing information, and supplier documentation within the ERP system.
  • Review open purchase orders and help identify potential material shortages, late deliveries, and other supply risks.
  • Assist with expediting critical materials to support production schedules and customer commitments.

 

Shipping and Receiving

  • Support receiving activities by verifying incoming materials against purchase orders, packing slips, certifications, and inspection requirements.
  • Assist with labeling, documenting, and routing received materials to inspection, stock, production, or quarantine areas.
  • Help prepare domestic and international shipments, including packaging, shipping documentation, carrier coordination, and tracking.
  • Maintain accurate shipping and receiving records in accordance with company procedures and aerospace quality requirements.
  • Assist with investigating shipping discrepancies, damaged goods, incorrect quantities, and missing documentation.

 

Supplier Management

  • Support supplier communication regarding order acknowledgments, delivery schedules, quality documentation, and corrective actions.
  • Assist in maintaining supplier performance data, including on-time delivery, quality performance, lead times, and responsiveness.
  • Help organize supplier records, certifications, approvals, and compliance documentation.
  • Participate in supplier review meetings and assist with follow-up actions as assigned.
  • Support efforts to identify alternate suppliers and mitigate supply-chain risks.

 

Inventory Control

  • Assist with cycle counts, physical inventory activities, and reconciliation of inventory variances.
  • Help maintain accurate inventory records, location data, and material traceability in the ERP system.
  • Monitor inventory levels and support replenishment planning for critical materials and consumables.
  • Assist with identifying excess, obsolete, damaged, or slow-moving inventory.
  • Support material movement and warehouse organization to improve inventory accuracy and operational efficiency.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

 

  • Currently pursuing a degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Management, Operations Management, Logistics, or related field.

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Strong interest in supply chain operations within aerospace, manufacturing, defense, or other regulated industries.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including formulas, pivot tables, and data analysis tools.
  • Familiarity with ERP systems such as Costpoint, SAP, Oracle, or similar is preferred.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work independently and in a team environment.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with procurement, warehouse, quality, production, engineering, and supplier teams.
  • Basic understanding of inventory management, purchasing, logistics, or manufacturing processes is preferred.
  • Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office Tools: Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
  • Eagerness to learn and take initiative.

 

Special remarks regarding work environment, if applicable

  • This position is located in Mojave, CA
  • This position may involve work in both an office setting and a warehouse or manufacturing environment. The intern may be required to safely handle, move, and organize materials in accordance with company procedures and applicable safety requirements.
  • $20.00 Hourly 
  • 9/80 Schedule

Base salary and leveling are established on a case-by-case basis. We consider several factors to ensure a competitive offer, including your location, educational background, and a comprehensive assessment of the skills and experience demonstrated during your interviews.</

Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

Building breakthrough technology requires strong teams and operations behind it. Our Business Operations and Program Management teams work across Tenstorrent to solve complex business challenges, improve how we operate, and help teams execute and scale.

 

What You Might Work On:
This posting spans multiple teams across Tenstorrent’s business operations functions. We make the process simple for you — one application, one recruiter screen — then match you to the specific team and opportunity that best fits your interests and experience.

  • Human Resources: Support people programs and operations across the employee lifecycle, including AI & systems, employee experience, organizational initiatives, and process improvement.
  • Finance: Support financial planning, reporting, budgeting, analysis, and projects that help teams understand business performance and make informed decisions.
  • Supply Chain: Support planning, sourcing, supplier coordination, logistics, and operational processes that help move products from development through production and delivery.
  • Strategic Operations: Support high-impact cross-functional initiatives through research, analysis, project management, process improvement, and coordination across teams.
  • Program Management: Drive cross-functional planning, tracking, risk management, and execution across technical and operational teams to ensure initiatives deliver on schedule and strategic goals.

Locations: Santa Clara, CA · Toronto,ON

 

Who You Are

  • Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Business, Finance, Economics, Human Resources, Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, or a related field.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong communicator who can work effectively across different teams and stakeholders.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with evolving priorities.
  • Interested in understanding how different business functions work together to help a technology company scale.

What We Need

  • Ability to take ambiguous business or operational problems and turn them into clear, actionable next steps.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple priorities and follow through on deliverables.
  • Comfort working with data, spreadsheets, reporting, and/or project-management tools.
  • Ability to communicate information, progress, risks, and recommendations clearly.
  • Collaborative mindset and willingness to work across functions.

What You Will Learn

  • How business functions support the development and growth of a deep-tech company.
  • How teams use data and operational insights to make decisions and improve processes.
  • How cross-functional programs and projects move from planning through execution.
  • How HR, Finance, Supply Chain, Strategic Operations, Engineering, and Product collaborate across the organization.
  • How scalable processes are built in a rapidly growing company.
 

USA Hiring Timelines

This internship opportunity is available throughout our 3 terms with the following corresponding recruitment cycles:

The United States is building nuclear power again, and The Nuclear Company is building the software that helps make it possible. NOS supports the regulatory, supply chain, cost, schedule, and field work behind reactor construction. 

As a Security Engineer Intern, you will join the Product Security team to help secure NOS and the cloud systems that support it. You will work with security and software engineers on meaningful projects across application security, cloud security, and governance, risk, and compliance (GRC). You might help assess a new product feature from a security perspective, strengthen a cloud control, improve a detection, or document evidence of compliance with a given cybersecurity framework. You will have a mentor and the opportunity to own a scoped project from design to delivery. 

This is a six-month Spring 2027 co-op based in Washington, DC, on-site three days a week.

Responsibilities 

  • Build scripts, tools, and automation that help engineering teams develop secure software. 
  • Help identify and address security risks in applications, APIs, AWS workloads, and development pipelines.

description:
About the Developer Experience team

The Developer Experience (DevX) team owns how developers learn and build on Together AI. We run the documentation site, API reference, quickstarts, cookbooks, and the tooling that keeps all of it accurate as the platform ships new models and features every week.

We treat docs as a product and as code. Content lives in Git, publishes through Mintlify, and stays in sync with the API through CI/CD automation built on GitHub Actions. We also write for two audiences at once: the human developer reading a guide, and the AI coding agent pulling our docs into its context window. That means a house style guide built for AI-assisted authoring, structured content agents can parse, and automated review passes that check drafts against our quality bar.

Role Overview

As a Technical Writer Intern on DevX, you will write, test, and ship documentation that thousands of developers use to build with open-weight models. You'll be paired with a DevX mentor and own significant projects end to end, from scoping through launch, with real users and real metrics at the finish line. 

This is a hands-on, technical role. You'll run the code you document, call our APIs, and open pull requests against the docs repo from your first week.

Potential projects include:

  • Build a closed-to-open migration kit
  • Make a docs section agent-ready, and prove it
  • Generate the CLI reference from source
  • Write an evaluation design tutorial series

Responsibilities

  • Write clear, accurate guides, tutorials, and reference content for Together AI's inference, fine-tuning, and GPU cluster products.
  • Work with engineers, product managers, and researchers to understand new features well enough to explain them simply.
  • Use AI tools in your daily workflow, and help us improve how we use them for drafting, editorial review, and publishing.
  • Test every feature you document by running the code yourself, and file bugs when the product or the docs don't behave as expected.
  • Draft, review, and publish in a docs-as-code workflow: Git, pull requests, code review, and Mintlify.
  • Contribute to release notes and changelog entries as features launch.
  • Use page analytics, search data, and developer feedback to decide what to improve next.

Qualifications

  • Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program in Computer Science, Technical Communication, or a related field, graduating December 2027 or later.
  • Exceptional written communication: you can make a complex technical idea clear and approachable.
  • Working knowledge of at least one programming language (Python or TypeScript preferred) and comfort with Git source control.
  • Curiosity about how developers learn, and how AI is changing the way they do it.

Nice to have

  • Experience calling an LLM API or building a small project with AI tools.
  • Familiarity with Markdown/MDX, static site generators, or docs platforms like Mintlify or Docusaurus.
  • Experience with CI tools such as GitHub Actions.

Writing sample

Your application should include one or two writing samples, representing what you think is your own best work. The subject doesn’t have to be technical, or even nonfiction—though both are a plus! For example:

  • A technical blog post.
  • A README, tutorial, or contribution to open-source docs.
  • A research paper.
  • A personal essay.
  • A school newspaper submission.

About Together AI

Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month.

We appreciate the individuality of the people around us.

 

JOB SUMMARY:

The Data and Analytics Engineer Intern will assist in designing, building, and testing data platforms and analytics solutions, including preparing trusted data for AI-enabled applications, to generate actionable insights for our customers.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT TO LEARN:

  • The challenges modern businesses are facing with data and how to address them with leading-edge technology solutions
  • How to break down complex data problems and solve them by designing simplified, achievable solutions
  • How organizations can leverage data to gain a competitive advantage by extracting patterns from large datasets
  • How to build and test data pipelines that prepare structured and unstructured data for analytics and AI use cases

  • Candidates should be pursuing a field of study applicable to the Data & Analytics internship

  • Academic or professional/internship experience working in a professional setting is a plus
  • Foundational knowledge of SQL or Python, data transformation, data modeling, or data visualization through coursework, personal projects, or prior experience is a plus
  • Exposure to cloud data platforms, notebooks, Git-based version control, or APIs is a plus
  • Interest in AI-enabled analytics and familiarity with data quality, metadata, privacy, and responsible use of AI tools; coursework or personal projects are welcome
  • Ability to work independently on assigned tasks and accepts direction on given assignments
  • Self-motivated individuals with a customer mindset and desire to help people
  • Enthusiasm for technical problem solving with attention to detail and strong communication skills
  • Ability to learn and research in a dynamic and engaging environment
  • Availability to work 40 hours per week throughout the internship

 

Actual salary will be based on a variety of factors, including location, experience, skill set, performance, licensure and certification, and business needs. The range for this position in other geographic locations may differ. Certain positions may also be eligible for variable incentive compensation, such as bonuses or commissions, that is not included in the base salary.

About Us:

Launched in 2011, Twitch is a global community that comes together each day to create multiplayer entertainment: unique, live, unpredictable experiences created by the interactions of millions. We bring the joy of co-op to everything, from casual gaming to world-class esports to anime marathons, music, and art streams. Twitch also hosts TwitchCon, where we bring everyone together to celebrate, learn, and grow their personal interests and passions. We’re always live at Twitch. Stay up to date on all things Twitch on Linkedin, X and on our Blog.

About the Role

**This internship is only for undergraduate students at North American colleges/universities with Winter 2027** We understand these can be flexible and if that’s the case, you can indicate on the application you want to be considered for both. No need to apply to both roles.

At Twitch, we’re always looking for high-potential talent. If you’re a current student in computer science, we’d love to see you apply. See below for just a few reasons why our cohort-based internship program is one-of-a kind.

Project-Based Learning at Scale: Twitch operates at a massive scale, requiring us to push the boundaries of technology and experiment with techniques used by only the largest websites. As an intern, you’ll have the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging engineering problems in the industry, making every project a valuable learning experience. 

Comprehensive Support Team: To ensure our interns thrive, we provide a dedicated support system, including a Manager, Mentor, and Early Careers Advisor. This team will work closely with you to guide your project from start to finish and ensure you have the resources needed to succeed. 

Enriched Intern Community: In addition to hands-on engineering work, you will participate in leadership and interpersonal development curriculum, as well as gain valuable industry insights from Twitch leaders through fireside chats. To complement the technical aspects of the program, we offer a variety of enrichment activities, including cohort trips, weekly advisory sessions, and local community events. We also provide housing assistance to make your summer internship as rewarding and enjoyable as possible.

description:
The Organization 

At USAFacts, we believe facts deserve to be heard. We turn data from thousands of jurisdictions into clear, unbiased answers about how government spends money and what it achieves. No political agenda. No commercial motive. Just public service.

Founded and funded by Steve Ballmer, former CEO of Microsoft, we work alongside Ballmer Group Philanthropy and Rainier Climate on civic impact.

As an intern, you’ll join a collaborative, mission-driven team and learn how complex public data becomes something the American people can actually use.

To top it off, Fast Company has recognized USAFacts four years running, including the 2026 Most Innovative Companies list. Learn more at usafacts.org and LinkedIn. Learn more about us at usafacts.org and linkedin.com/company/usafacts.

We’d love for you to bring your curiosity, and your conviction that facts matter, to your summer with us.

Your Internship with USAFacts

This is a paid, full-time internship for your penultimate year of undergraduate study, where you’ll do real work on real products. Here’s what to expect:

Pay

$38 per hour for at least 10 weeks, which comes to roughly $15,200 before taxes at 40 hours per week. Interns are overtime eligible, so hours over 40 per week are paid at time and a half.

Housing support

Relocating interns receive company-paid furnished corporate housing and a $1,000 travel reimbursement. Interns who live in the area and don’t need corporate housing can be reimbursed up to $2,000 per month for housing costs with a current rental agreement.

Paid sick days and holidays

3 paid sick days and paid holidays for the duration of your internship.

Hybrid schedule

In the office Tuesday through Thursday, with lunches provided, and the flexibility to work remotely or in-office the rest of the week.

Transportation

You’ll receive either an ORCA card for local public transit or paid parking in or near the building.

Events, community, and opportunities

At USAFacts, we believe a great internship is about more than just the work. Throughout the summer, you'll have opportunities to connect with your fellow interns, build relationships across the organization, and make the most of your time in the Seattle area. From organization-wide events and team outings to boat rides, paddleboarding adventures, and sushi dinners, you'll have plenty of opportunities to build connections and have fun along the way. description: Latent Reasoning for Tabular Foundation Models: Performance Enhancement and Interpretability Ekimetrics is the European leader in data science, with over 500 data scientists and 1,000+ projects since 2006. With offices in Paris, London, New York, and Hong Kong, we conduct projects in over 50 countries across various sectors, including financial services, retail, telecom, healthcare, and more. Our mission is to help companies audit their data opportunities, enhance their analytical capital, and deploy actionable solutions that maximize their marketing and operational performance while reinvigorating business models. Our absolute focus is on delivering short-term gains while ensuring the long-term development of our clients' data capital. We are committed to offering the most advanced data science approaches and building ethical, sustainable AI practices. Key Figures 20 years of experience in data science 500+ data scientists, all consultants 5 offices in Paris, London, New York, Hong Kong, and Shanghai 350+ clients (CAC40, Fortune500) $1M+ in profit generated for our clients since 2006 1,000+ data science projects Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem. A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack. Internship Objective: From Latent Reasoning to Better and More Understandable Tabular Models Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) such as TabPFN, TabICL or TabDPT are transformers pre-trained on large collections of mostly synthetic datasets. They learn in context: the training data and the points to predict are given as input, and predictions come out of a single forward pass, with no dataset-specific training or tuning. They now rival gradient boosting on many benchmarks [3], which is changing how tabular modeling is practiced. In large language models, a growing line of research lets the model “reason” in its latent space rather than through generated tokens, using extra depth-wise computation, reused continuous hidden states or internal iterations. This latent reasoning can improve performance without longer text outputs [1, 2]. Our hypothesis is that a similar mechanism can improve TFMs: spending more latent compute at inference on hard or ambiguous cases could help them make better use of the in-context examples. Almost all existing work on latent reasoning targets natural language, and its transfer to tabular models, whose architecture, pre-training data and output differ profoundly, remains largely unexplored. Mechanistic interpretability is starting to open the black box, both for latent-reasoning language models and for TFMs themselves [4]. It lets us ask not only whether latent reasoning improves a TFM, but also what the model actually computes during these extra steps, and whether that computation is faithful and useful. The internship therefore has two goals: designing and evaluating latent reasoning mechanisms for TFMs, and using interpretability methods to analyze what they learn. The intern will work with senior researchers and data scientists. This internship offers an opportunity to contribute to an emerging research topic at the intersection of tabular modeling, latent reasoning and interpretability. Key Responsibilities The intern will: Review the literature on latent reasoning (NLP) and tabular foundation models, building on recent surveys. Identify and adapt latent reasoning mechanisms to TFM architectures (e.g. iterative depth-wise computation, hidden-state reuse). Implement them on open-source TFMs and measure their effect on accuracy, calibration and robustness against strong baselines (gradient boosting, standard TFMs) at comparable compute. Apply interpretability methods (representation analysis, probing, activation patching) to characterize the computation performed during latent reasoning. Build an evaluation protocol on diverse tabular datasets, including realistic business cases. Document the results and contribute to scientific publications. Profile Currently in the final year of a Master’s or Engineering degree, with strong foundations in machine learning, statistics, and programming. Good grasp of model validation: train/test splits, data leakage, baselines. Strong analytical skills and the ability to work autonomously on an open-ended research problem. Knowledge of transformers and language models; familiarity with latent reasoning or recurrent-depth models is a plus. Strong Python and PyTorch skills, and a solid command of the standard data science toolkit (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, gradient-boosting libraries). Fluency in English is a plus. Nice to have: experience in interpretability, knowledge of TabPFN, TabICL or TabDPT, and solid software engineering practices (git, code review, testing). Benefits Hands-on Research & Engineering Experience: Build a pioneering agentic system on real data science workflows, contributing to a tool with direct real-world impact. Collaborative Learning: Engage with a team of data scientists, AI experts, and PhDs in a dynamic, research-driven environment within Ekimetr

With offices in Paris, London, New York, and Hong Kong, we conduct projects in over 50 countries across various sectors, including financial services, retail, telecom, healthcare, and more. Key Figures 20 years of experience in data science 500+ data scientists, all consultants 5 offices in Paris, London, New York, Hong Kong, and Shanghai 350+ clients (CAC40, Fortune500) $1M+ in profit generated for our clients since 2006 1,000+ data science projects Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem. A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack. Internship Objective: From a Business Question to a Trusted Recommendation LLM-based agents have made rapid progress in the past two years: they can now write, run and tune machine learning code with little human help. Yet real data science projects rarely start from a clean, well-defined task. They start from a business question and imperfect data, and the early choices (what to predict, how to measure success, how to validate) decide whether the result can be trusted. Automating these steps calls for assistants that know when to ask, when to stop, and how to back every claim with evidence. The Innovation Department is building remit , a harness that semi-automates the data science workflow. At each step of a project (framing, data design, exploratory analysis, modeling, evaluation), AI agents draft the output, automatic checks catch common mistakes such as data leakage, and a data scientist reviews and accepts the result before moving on. Ultimately, a business user brings a question and a dataset, and the system frames the problem, prepares and explores the data, compares models against a simple baseline, and returns a clear recommendation in which every figure can be traced back to the data. The work builds on recent research in agentic data science [1]. Agents now earn medals on many of the Kaggle competitions in MLE-bench [2], yet they tend to guess silently rather than ask when a task is ambiguous [3]. The Mission We are working to create general-purpose robots capable of accomplishing a wide variety of dexterous tasks with humans. To do this, our team is exploring how Large Behavior Models and other general-purpose machine learning models use generative AI techniques to produce robot actions from sensor data and human interactions. We use both simulation and human-interactive data to augment real-world robot data towards such embodied AI policies. The Challenge We envision a future where robots assist with household chores and cooking, aid older individuals in maintaining their independence, and enable people to spend more time on the activities they enjoy most. To achieve this, robots need to be able to operate reliably in messy, unstructured environments. Our mission is to answer the question “What will it take to create truly general-purpose robots that can accomplish a wide variety of tasks in settings like human homes with minimal human supervision?” We believe that the answer lies in using large-scale datasets of physical interaction from a variety of sources and building on the latest advances in machine learning to learn general-purpose robot behaviors from this data. The Internship We are seeking a research intern to join our Human Aware Interaction and Learning (HAIL) team. The research conducted on this internship aligns with our broader mission and will focus on one or more of the following areas at the intersection of robot learning and human-robot interaction (HRI): Data-efficient and general algorithms for learning robust multimodal policies that can also reason over actions in the presence of a human. This research would examine what additional features should be modeled when humans are present in the scene, or in collaborative scenarios, including how roles are shared and reallocated between the human and the robot. Developing hierarchical reasoning frameworks for learned robot policies that can reason over human and shared task states (intent, cues, roles) in order to enable fluent human-robot collaboration. Robustifying data-driven robot policies to the presence of humans, particularly in the low-data regimes typical of HRI, including approaches for data aggregation and simulative approaches towards adaptation of vision-language-action (VLA) models to human-human and/or human-robot interaction datasets. Uncertainty-aware teaming: estimating and calibrating when a learned policy will succeed given human context, and using such estimates to decide how the robot should act in a collaborative setting. Exploring additional data sources when training human-interactive robot policies, including human-human and synthetic/semi-synthetic data, towards novel datasets/methodologies and algorithmic frameworks that enable robots to efficiently learn from collaborative demonstrations, and better understand human behavior within these collaborations. Developing shared autonomy in conjunction with VLA models to create more sophisticated fusion between autonomous and manual control beyond simple switching mechanisms. This could be studied both in the context of efficiently collecting data and runtime decision-making approaches. The intern who joins our team will be expected to create working code prototypes, interact frequently with team members, run experiments with both simulated and real (physical) robots, and participate in publishing the work to peer-reviewed venues. We’re looking for an intern who is comfortable working with both existing large static datasets and helping build and maintain a new corpus of robot data.

The Team Our team in the Robotics division is developing pretrained generalist policies that can support a broad range of tasks, environments, and robotic systems. A central scientific challenge is determining how these broadly pretrained policies can be efficiently adapted to new target tasks while achieving the reliability, precision, and robustness required for real-world use. Pretraining can provide a policy with broad behavioral capabilities, but those capabilities may not immediately translate into dependable performance in a specific deployment setting. Effective post-training methods are therefore essential for converting general capabilities into policies that can adapt quickly, learn from limited additional data or interaction, and perform consistently on demanding downstream tasks. The Opportunity Our research interests include reinforcement learning, imitation learning, human-in-the-loop learning, simulation, world models, policy distillation, and large-scale robot learning. We aim to advance the scientific foundations of policy adaptation while developing methods that may ultimately be evaluated or deployed within internal research projects involving real-world industrial tasks. Potential research directions include, but are not limited to: Offline-to-online reinforcement learning DAgger, imitation learning, and human-in-the-loop policy improvement Sim-to-real policy distillation and adaptation Policy improvement, planning, or data generation using world models Data-efficient adaptation to new tasks and environments
